title: Paid once, two orders
fullTitle: You Clicked Pay Once. Why Did the App Create Two Orders?

scenes.narration: One tap on Pay. Two orders in the database. The customer did not click twice. The app treated every request as a new intention.
captions: One tap on Pay. Two orders in the database.
The app treated every request as a new intention.

scenes.narration: Follow the first request. It reaches the server, passes validation, and the database commits order one. From the server's view, the work is done.
captions: The first request reaches the server. The database commits order 1.
From the server's view, the work is done.

scenes.narration: Then the response is lost. Here the server deliberately destroys the socket after the commit. The client sees a network error and cannot know whether the order exists. No network gives you exactly-once delivery.
captions: The response is lost after the commit (controlled fault).
The client sees a network error and cannot know if the order exists.
No network gives you exactly-once delivery.

scenes.narration: So the client retries. Disabling the button would not have helped: this is a retry after an error, not a double click.
captions: The client retries.
Disabling the button would not help: this is a retry, not a double click.

scenes.narration: The vulnerable endpoint has no memory of the first request. It inserts again. Two attempts, two orders.
captions: The vulnerable endpoint has no memory of the first request.
Two attempts, two orders.

scenes.narration: The repair: one idempotency key per checkout attempt, reused on every retry, scoped to the session user and the operation, never a client-supplied user ID. Validated fields are normalised into a fingerprint. Order and key record are written in one transaction, and a unique constraint makes the first writer win. No check-then-insert race.
captions: Fix: one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt, reused on retries.
Scoped to the session user and operation; fingerprint of validated fields.
Order + key record in ONE transaction; UNIQUE makes the first writer win.

scenes.narration: Same scenario: commit, lose the response, retry with the same key. The second request finds the stored record and returns the original result.
captions: Retest: commit, lose the response, retry with the same key.
The second request finds the stored record and returns the original result.

scenes.narration: Two attempts, one order. Same key, different quantity: four twenty-two. Five concurrent requests, one key: one order. Two separate purchases need two separate keys.
captions: Two attempts, one order.
Same key, different payload: 422. Five concurrent, one key: one order.
Two separate purchases need two separate keys.

scenes.narration: A new request is not always a new intention. Two limits: the transaction covers the local database, not an external payment provider; and expired key records let a late enough retry count as new.
captions: A new request is not always a new intention.
Limits: the transaction does not cover an external payment provider.
Expired key records let a late enough retry count as new.
